methodological_rigor.justification: GEMINI is a prospective real-world evaluation of 10,889 women in one UK screening region, with routine double reading maintained, live AI additional review, and prespecified simulations of 17 workflows. The primary workflow, operating points, evaluation plan, and statistical analysis plan were specified before data collection or analysis, and a predetermined sample size targeted 65 positives with 91.5% power, ultimately yielding 106 confirmed positives. Strengths include independent analysis in a trusted research environment, vendor separation, blinded routine readers to AI opinions, and a sensitivity analysis for fewer additional cancers. Limitations include single-region evaluation of one AI system, simulated triage workflows, 29.1% unsent images due to an IT error, 10.4% AI exclusions, and absent interval-cancer follow-up.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a prospective cohort/service evaluation with paired comparison to routine double reading rather than an RCT, supporting Oxford level 2b. The clinical relevance is very high because it evaluates breast cancer screening workflows in routine care, detecting 11 additional cancers and modeling cancer detection, recall, PPV, sensitivity, specificity, and workload. The lack of interval-cancer follow-up prevents definitive sensitivity and overdiagnosis conclusions, but the operational and patient-care implications are immediate.

reporting_quality.justification: STARD-AI is explicitly stated and is the appropriate standard for diagnostic AI evaluation. The manuscript reports participant flow, inclusion/exclusion, AI operating points, index-test integration, reference outcome definition, prespecified endpoints, confidence intervals, noninferiority/superiority gates, and reader-workload calculations. Important limitations are transparently reported, including missing interval-cancer follow-up, simulated triage assumptions, and AI-ineligible cases. Source data and runnable R code on Zenodo are referenced, but patient-level screening data are held in a secure environment rather than openly deposited.

novelty_literature.justification: Prospective AI breast-screening evaluations already exist, including MASAI and ScreenTrustCAD, so the general concept is not first-in-class. GEMINI's novelty is in combining live AI additional reading with prespecified simulations of 17 workflow configurations to match different screening-service priorities. The study also contributes UK-specific, real-world evidence using a commercial AI system while preserving routine care. Its novelty is therefore mainly methodological and implementation-focused rather than algorithmic.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is unusually clear for a workflow evaluation, with the abstract reporting cohort size, intervention, additional cancers, primary workflow effects, and workload savings. Methods are organized around sample, AI system, study design, data processing, independence, statistical analysis, and predetermined sample size. Tables and figure captions make the 17 workflow comparisons, workload components, participant flow, and testing gates interpretable. The discussion directly addresses single-site design, simulated workflows, AI exclusions, technical failures, and lack of interval-cancer follow-up.

key_strengths: Prospective real-world screening evaluation with 10,889 women and routine standard-of-care double reading preserved.
Prespecified primary workflow, operating points, evaluation plan, statistical analysis plan, and sample-size calculation.
Independent analysis environment separated from the AI vendor, with routine readers blinded to AI opinions.
Clinically and operationally meaningful endpoints include cancer detection, recall, PPV, sensitivity, specificity, and workload across 17 workflows.
key_concerns: Single UK region and one AI system limit generalizability.
Triage workflows are simulated and assume reader performance would not change under altered workload.
Interval-cancer follow-up is not yet available, so true sensitivity and downstream clinical impact remain uncertain.
A technical issue prevented AI assessment for 4,992 attending women, and the AI excluded 1,260 examinations.
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study has high immediate relevance, strong prospective design, prespecification, and transparent limitations. Tier 1 with minor revisions is plausible because it addresses a practice-facing screening question with unusually complete workflow evidence, although longer follow-up and broader validation are still needed.
